name: Sandwalking

sections.body:
Fremen survival depends on knowing when the desert can hear them. Sandwalking reduces the disturbance made by personal movement across open sand, giving a practiced traveler more room to cross between safe ground and distant work.

It is a movement discipline. Harvesting spice, running machinery and creating other noise remain separate risks, however carefully the worker approaches.
sections.title: Crossing without a rhythm

sections.body:
Sandwalking ranges from level 0 to 20. The Fremen sietch start gives each survivor a level between 10 and 15, representing an existing knowledge of desert travel. Further practice improves the movement-vibration multiplier.

Check the least experienced person in a party when planning a crossing. Quiet movement by one expert does not erase the disturbance made by everyone else.
sections.title: Training and starting skill

sections.body:
An untrained walker produces the full personal movement signal. At level 5 the multiplier is 0.90; at 10 it is 0.70; at 15 it is 0.40. It falls to 0.20 at 18, 0.10 at 19 and zero at level 20, with intermediate levels following the skill curve.

At mastery, personal walking produces no wormsign. This benefit ends with walking: even a master still needs to judge a noisy harvest or an active thumper.
sections.title: How skill changes vibration

sections.body:
Sandwalking does not silence extractors, spice harvesting, explosions, thumpers or shield emissions. It does not change sand into refuge or protect a pawn caught in a committed breach.

Use skill together with short work periods, clear retreat routes and genuine rock. It makes desert travel less conspicuous while leaving the consequences of noisy work intact.
sections.title: Working in Maker country

code.purpose: Sandwalking level curve and Fremen start range
Applies sandwalking skill to movement vibration

summary: Sandwalking breaks the rhythm of a person’s passage across open sand. Practice reduces the vibration that draws a Maker, allowing more careful movement between islands of rock.
